The irony being of course in BJ And The Bear that it was a monkey not a bear.

Because she looks like the sort of woman that would work in say a photocopying shop.
And she'd probably be quite charmed by me and stuff.

[smooth DJ voice] "Will the overweight aunt in the purple dress please now take the floor with a little unfortunate kid...
"As the dance floor is currently empty, will any eight-year-old boys wearing those tiny tuxedos please slide across the dance floor on their knees...
...until they are taken home and put to bed early."

Whether there was a sit-down meal

A cummerbund. I said "do I need a cummerbund?". He said "Well...you gonna be dancing?"

I just love the idea of him being at some kind of do and "right Elaine, jackets off, cummerbunds on, time for a dance".

They were born on the same day.

I didn't say they were born on the same day, did I?

Yeah, i remember that. i remember that. shops shut. and you couldn't get aspirin and stuff, certain things...
Exactly, nightmare on a sunday afternoon
Yeah that's right, yeah, pubs didn't open til 12 did they?
Oh, do you remember space hoppers?
Yeah. yeah, shut up. can i ask you something?

Ever since I've known you, you've seemed to think that's the case cause you've watched all the "Rocky" films--
And you think, "That's fair enough. That seems straightforward enough." But look at your physique. Yeah, you've got some upper body strength--
But, you know, you've also got some up- some lower belly strength, as well, I've noticed.

Going back in time, rewinding the past.

Your usual table? Can I just ask you two questions Godfather? One is, have we won a prize tonight? Two, can you have someone iced for me?
It’s ludicrous, what do you suddenly got over all these people? When did you suddenly become the daddy?
Well I came from nowhere, and y’know, I got Polaroid’s of all the head of all the stations. Yeah, exactly.

q: Ricky banished Steve from the bed to a tiny hotel box chair for the whole England match. Why was Steve especially furious?
a: It was his own hotel room
x: He'd paid for the whole minibar
The chair faced away from the telly
Ricky had eaten all the room service
f: "It's 90 bloody minutes plus the intermission. It was my room. I was furious." At his size, "those tiny little crappy hotel box chairs are no good."

ex: No, big man. And so I just thought, let's pop the pillows down. That wasn't enough. I said, Steve, I can't do this. I can't watch football with a man on a bed. I said, so go in the chair.
And he sat in this chair!
So I sat in the chair which is, if you're a man of my size, those tiny little crappy hotel box chairs are no good. It's 90 bloody minutes plus the intermission. It was my room. I was furious.

q: Steve said Karl was imagining the ageing girl's life like which music video?
a: The Fat Boy Slim one where something crawls out of the sea and evolves

The Peter Gabriel one with stop-motion dancing fruit
The Radiohead one where a man lies down on the pavement

ex: I think you’re thinking of her life like that Fat Boy Slim video where it starts off as something crawling out of the sea and then it evolves really quickly over three minutes. I mean, that’s not the case, Karl. Her mind isn’t- she isn’t…
She’s not living a life, a whole life, in like, you know, three weeks. It’s just her body is-is degenerating quicker than it should.

q: Spotting Dr. Fox at number 39 on the radio "Power List", what did Steve joke had helped him up it?
a: His medical qualifications
f: Ricky agreed: "that sneaks him up the list, yeah." Ricky himself was 56th.
ex: Just checking to see, uh- oh, yeah, Dr. Fox. Good, he’s on there at number thirty-nine. I’m assuming his medical qualifications have also pitched in in the--
Yeah, that’s the- yeah, that sneaks him up the list, yeah.

q: Steve's sister photographed a factory worker's self-designed tattoo that covered his whole back. What did it show?

ex: You're not far off, I'll tell you what it was. He had this tattooed on his back, it took up his entire back, she took a photo of it for me. He drew it himself, he had it tattooed himself and it was just too much detail, too much detail for…
It was a naked female vampire, having a shower.
Why was she having a shower?
Well that's why she was naked.

q: Steve brought in a Pink Floyd CD and it kept skipping on air. What did he blame?

Karl scratching it with a fork

ex: I dunno, because that always plays fine on my home system, so I don't if it's something that Sturgess has done. You haven't got your big, greasy thumbprints over it, have you?
(his mouth seems to be full) It's ya teeth...
'Cause I saw you a, a huge hog roast as uh, as I came in.
And throwing the bones behind her.

ex: Have you had one, Steve? An anxiety dream?
Anxiety dreams? I do have them periodically, yeah. Used to be a lot of things like running to get to school on time, but suddenly your feet are running in treacle and you can her the school bell--
I haven’t had them for years. I just haven’t had an anxiety dream for years and years and years. Yeah, dunno. Don’t care.

Well no, you just genuinely don’t care about anything this is the problem. You’ve just got to a point now where nothing bothers you. It’s like you’re too lazy and disinterested in anything: this show; your career; my career; Karl’s--

q: After Steve read out emails saying Rockbusters had run its course, what did Karl predict Steve would come in with next week?
a: Another hip hop track full of effin' and jeffin'

A phone-in about tall people's problems

ex: Alright, well we’ll see what you come up with next week. Let’s see what you do, see what you come in with.
I’m guessing you’ll be popping in with another hip hop track--

q: On XFM, Steve admitted that when strangers ask him for directions he pretends to be foreign. Why?
a: He's terrified of giving them the wrong directions
x: He's sick of tourists stopping him
He once got lost leading a tour group
f: Steve's fear is they'll "come back and find you and go, 'You led us astray'." So now he just affects a foreign accent.
ex: It's the same thing if someone asks me for directions, I always pretend I'm foreign. I always go, (Foreign Accent) "I don't, umm--"
I can't- cuz I- I- just terrified of giving them the wrong directions and then--
Well, just say, "I don't know, I don't live- from- here".
I don't like- cuz I sort of, you know- I feel bad. Cuz I- what I used to, sort of, give directions cuz I like giving directions, I like helping people out. But then I realized I didn't really know--
You hang- you used to hang around going, "You all right?" "Yeah, we're fine, yeah." "Do you want to know where to go?"
I tend to have a go even if I don't know.
Exactly. But it's- I'm always terrified they'll come back and find you and go, "You led us astray".

q: Steve gave Karl a bottle for Christmas. Why wasn't it the champagne they got free from the BBC?
a: That was far too good for Karl, so he got sparkling wine
x: Steve was saving it for his mum

ex: Yeah, that's not the champagne we got free from the BBC, is it?
It's not, actually, no, Rick because, umm, that is far too good for the likes of Karl.
And I wasn't going to give it to him - he wouldn't appreciate it. That's just sparkling wine.
Oh, brilliant. Oh, he'll love that.
Yeah, he- well, he doesn't really know the difference.

q: Terrified of being mugged when he moved to London, how many wallets did Steve carry around for about two months?
a: Three, two of them fake
f: He gave up because a mugger handed two fake wallets would be "twice as angry", and might run up fines on the old library cards inside.
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Law and Order · 2009
ex: -which had some sort of old library cards and DVD cards - you know - video shop cards and stuff, and like I put a fiver in there, you know. And then I got really anxious because I thought, what if I hand over my fake wallet? And he goes…

Two of which were fake. Right? And then, do you know the reason I stopped? Because I thought, what if he-I give him both fake wallets? I give him one fake wallet, he opens it, he goes, well, this is fake wallet. I give him the second fake…

q: Since everything annoys Ricky, where had Steve said Ricky should be locked up?
a: In a tower, like princesses in fairytales

In the stocks on a village green
In a monastery with a vow of silence

ex: Yeah, I know you're happy with Suzanne and everything but apart from that, you're never happy. You are the most grumpy, moany thing in the world. I mean, I get annoyed but I'm always happy. I was annoyed here, I was happy coming here but…

...I'm just annoyed. You are just like "Uhh, the worlds on me. It's rubbish, this." I know the world's great, it's just sometimes people annoy me by being there. You know, but uhh... Steve said I should be locked in one of those towers…
In fairytales. Because eveyrthing annoys me. Umm. But you are... You're grumpy.

q: Ricky asked Steve whether he'd rather be homeless in Liverpool or London. Where did Steve pick instead?
a: The Algarve
f: Ricky reckoned the man was going for the "double sympathy vote": "I'm homeless and I'm a Liverpudlian."
ex: Well he might have been homeless in Liverpool and thought if...
Well, where would you rather be homeless Liverpool or London?

ex: You know those people that, you see them on the street, they’re selling fags duty free, obviously, and they’re just selling them on the street. Have you ever seen these--

I walk down Finchley Road a lot because it’s near my place and all the people there, they’re sort of, eh, looking a bit shifty, and then they just, they think that you’re maybe a smoker. They just, you know, fags in their jacket and it’ll…
They won’t go up to you, though, would they?
They know you must never have had a fag in your life--

ex: So you spent Most of this, the 80s, running around London and collecting debris and making your home outfit. You sound like a womble.
Yeah, but I wasn't shaped like one until I was 32.
And, you know, this is kind of. You were making everything except a living.

a: Only the lender gets to say "don't worry about it"

ex: Oh hang on. I forget the one where we had an argument over 50p. Went out for coffee-
Yeah you didn’t want to give me the 50p back that you owed me.
That was the same day you’d given him about 40 quids worth of lager.

But see, this is my problem, this is my point at the time. It’s not, the 50p in terms of money is not what’s important. The fact that you think you don’t have to give me money back because it’s only 50p, that was the point at stake. It’s…
I don’t want to fall out about it.

f: Ricky also pointed out there were some gigs "he doesn't even turn up to." Karl: "Yeah, we won't even go on about that."
ex: I’ve sorted you out tickets for gigs.
Some he doesn’t even turn up to.
Yeah, we won’t even go on about that. Alright? Lager.
You sorted him out with The Cure, he complained it was boring.

He wanted to learn about it himself

ex: Did I just try and explain determinism to Carl Pilkington?
Yeah, I didn't want to stop you.
But I mean, what. What am I thinking?
It just made you look. You look more of an idiot than you.
I know, exactly. Yeah. I feel stupid.

a: Thin mats like teenage gymnasts use on Blue Peter

And I’m looking down at this, I’m thinking now… they may as well have shouted up, “If you fall you’re done for, but we might be able to protect the equipment.” You know what I mean, it was so rubbish.

q: Almost halfway through the first hour, having talked only about nudity and todgers, who did Steve sarcastically say he was looking forward to hearing the show?

Jonathan Ross and the Comedy Awards panel

So, excellent work from us. Well done lads.
I'm looking forward to Dr. Fox and the rest of the Sony Award committee listening to this one.

I thought this was the most famous foreign film for years, it won Oscars, it was a huge film, everyone knew it was foreign, she goes and it went, the credit begins, it says Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, she went 'stupid name for a…

q: Steve gave which song as an example of one ruined by being used on a Coke advert?

That song 'First Time' which was on the Coke ad (singing) “First time, first love”, ruined now cos that was on a Coke advert.
Was that, wasn't that Four Non Blondes
It was Robin Givens, wasn't it?

"...more than his films? Buy the poster!"
f: Karl had already muttered "Oh, forget it" at Ricky's version. After Steve's tagline he added: "I can't be bothered."

q: Steve read from one of Nelson's love letters to Lady Hamilton. Besides not eating or sleeping, what did Nelson say he never touched?
a: Even pudding
f: Nelson's words: "I can neither eat nor sleep for thinking of you my dearest love. I never touch, even pudding." Ricky's verdict: "That's a euphemism."
ex: Couple of quotes from there. Ahh, this is him writing to Lady Hamilton, who he's having an affair with. "I can neither eat nor sleep for thinking of you my dearest love. I never touch, even pudding."
I think we've all written a letter like that to a lady.

q: Karl moaned that everything shuts down from mid-December until early January. What did Steve sarcastically say Karl was missing out on?
a: Going to the library to catch up on all his reading
f: Steve's dig at Karl's busy schedule: "All that reading you've got to catch up on." Karl's reply: "I'm just saying that we're wasting time."
ex: Everyone shuts down by about December 15th or whatever, and then it doesn't get going again till like January 6.
But what is it you're missing out on during this period?
Just, it's like two weeks there. That's. I mean, that bit between Christmas and New Year. You might as well delete that out the calendar.
Yeah. Because heaven forbid, you can't put down the library because it's closed. All that reading you've got to catch up on.
I'm just saying that we're wasting time.

q: Karl's sort-of uncle Alf had a spare mattress but slept in a rubber dinghy. What was Steve's explanation?
a: He's terrified of flooding
x: He's training to row the Channel
He gets seasick on dry land
f: Alf also has two tellys: "One that works picture-wise and one that works for the sound."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The Earth · 2010
ex: He's the one who I've told you about two tellys, -we've talked about on the podcast- Two tellys. One that works picture-wise and one that works for the sound.
Slept in a rubber dinghy. Right? Now, the thing is...
He said "Yeah, yeah, yeah. Got mattress, come and get it." So I go round there
Why doesn't he sleep on the f***ing mattress if he's got one? Why is he sleeping in a f***ing boat if he's got a mattress?

ex: …a sort of hour-long workout. And I said to him, get one of the ones that’s hosted by like uhm…

…Elle Macpherson or Cindy Crawford, you know, you know, someone like that, someone sexy, right? So I swear to God, we went down this morning, we put it on, right? Just want you to picture this scene, right? It’s me, and my mate, in our…
…right? That was—“It was the cheapest one, Steve,” he told me. Thanks very much, mate.

I-I thought it was like she’d think, “Jesus Christ, I’ve never, I’ve never met anyone like him.”
And she- I remember the one time she accidentally walked in she went, “Oh! Oh, sorry. Wrong room.” and left again.

ex: That's partly it but also because I keep stand- hanging out by stacks of Office DVDs.
(Laughing) Wearing a t-shirt with a picture of you and me on it.

q: The woman who wrote the list emailed in. Why did she say Steve wasn't that unlikely a lust object after all?

He has a lovely radio voice

ex: "I wouldn't waste my time, the flaming cheek. Although it's a horrible picture I am of course in real life a vision of loveliness. I am not thirty-eight, I'm twenty-five. I don't think Steven's that unlikely lust object. A sense of…
A sense of humour's important. That's a downer, innit?

q: How did Steve hypothetically plan to get onto a nudist beach without stripping at the door?
a: Swim up to it in a wetsuit
x: Dig a tunnel under the dunes
Hide in an ice cream van

ex: Would it be possible for a bloke who was, say, a fairly good swimmer to swim up to the beach in a wetsuit--
Just say, just say for the sake of it that this person, you know, had some time on his hands for a week.

q: Ricky pointed out that Karl didn't have the facts either, and "he runs the radio station!" How did Steve correct him?
a: They just keep him there like a mascot

He's only there to water the plants
f: Steve said: "He's like a pet, isn't he? They have him runnin' around the office."

He doesn't run it, they keep him here like a mascot! He's like a pet, isn't he? They have him runnin' around the office.

q: A woman phoned in to tell Karl to stick up for himself, calling Steve 'so arrogant'. How did Steve correct her?
a: He's not arrogant, he's just mean and nasty
x: He's not arrogant, he's just shy
He's not arrogant, he's just honest
He's not arrogant, he's just tall
f: Steve said: "I'm just not a very nice person." He also said: "I'm not arrogant, I think I'm pathetic."
ex: I don't think I'm arrogant. I think I'm mean.
Just think I'm, sort of, objectionable. I don't think it's arrogance--
I think it's, sort of, nastiness.
I'm just (Laughing Slightly) not a very nice person.

q: Steve read about a man who died falling out of a window while mooning. What did he say would have been a better last gag to die after?
a: A two-hour impromptu Eddie Izzard-style routine
x: A whoopee cushion at a wedding
f: Ricky: "Mooning isn't funny enough." Steve: "It's just not a good enough gag." He called the death "almost karmic".
ex: No. It's just not a good enough gag.
Do you know what I mean? It's a witless sort of thing to do and then to be killed for it.
If you just done a two hour impromptu Eddie Izard-style routine and then you got tragically killed, that would sort of make sense.
But mooning, it's almost karmic because it's such a bad joke.

q: Aged 11 or 12, Steve and a friend hosted their own radio show from a bedroom. With no transmitter, how did they broadcast it?
a: Through speakers hidden in the bushes of the front garden
x: By shouting through the neighbours' letterboxes
Over the school tannoy at lunchtime
By posting cassette tapes round the street
